vectors.name: formats-xml/basic/interleaved-elements-preserve-order
vectors.comment: A map-of-arrays model cannot represent this interleaving; the edge list can. This is the whole reason the Document is an ordered edge list rather than a map -- confirmed against JSON's own parse of the equivalent {"m":[...]} shape, which cannot preserve this order at all.

vectors.name: formats-xml/basic/attributes-are-dropped-on-read
vectors.comment: D-3 (closed 2026-08-23): the attribute x="1" is gone -- there is no path from a Document edge back to an attribute, so writing never produces one either -- and that drop MUST now be reported via format.attribute-dropped (Sec8.3.8), not silent. Path is $.a: the element the attribute was lost from, the same convention format.float-special uses for the value it substituted.

vectors.name: formats-xml/basic/namespace-prefix-is-dropped-on-read
vectors.comment: D-3 (closed 2026-08-23): a prefixed tag <ns:b> reads as the local name b, with the prefix and any namespace binding discarded -- reported via format.namespace-dropped (Sec8.3.8), not silent. Path is $.a.b: the element the prefix was lost from, using the same RecordName.label-style dotted path convention Sec8.4 defines for Schema/Document paths generally.

vectors.name: formats-xml/basic/multi-rooted-document-cannot-be-written
vectors.comment: An XML document has exactly one top-level element; a Document with several top-level edges (legal in JSON/YAML/TOML) has no XML spelling at all. This is exactly why the worked examples in every format page wrap the Order under a single top-level `order` key -- XML alone requires it.

vectors.name: formats-xml/basic/label-with-illegal-xml-characters-cannot-be-written
vectors.comment: A space is not legal in an XML name, and there is no single well-defined substitute -- sanitizing it means inventing content, and (confirmed separately) can even make two genuinely different labels collide into the same written tag with no way to detect it happened. The write fails, unconditionally, not just under strict -- this is not a format.* adjustment a caller can opt out of checking for.
